history: 'The finest land of Jiangnan, the imperial state of Jinling.' Nanjing has 2,500 years of city history; six dynasties, the Southern Tang, Ming, Taiping and the Republic all made it their capital. Its 25 km of surviving Ming wall is the world's longest brick-stone city wall; Ming Xiaoling founded the imperial tomb style of Ming and Qing. Lantern shadows and oar sounds at the Confucius Temple on the Qinhuai River run back a thousand years. The plane-tree avenues are the city's gentlest card.
importance: Capital of Jiangsu · Ancient capital of six dynasties · First-batch National Historical City
foods: Salted duck at its plumy best in osmanthus season — white skin, tender meat.
Duck blood and vermicelli soup — the king of Nanjing snacks.
Jiming soup dumplings served upside down, brimming with broth.
Qijiawan potstickers — crispy base, juicy; bite carefully, it's hot.
Taro shoots slow-stewed in brown sugar and osmanthus — Jinling's sweet No.1.
Duck embryo egg — the brave eater's Nanjing delicacy.
A big bowl of pork-skin noodles piled high — the deluxe Nanjing breakfast.
Red-bean rice balls of Lianhu — sweet and warming.
Five-colored steamed cakes of the Confucius Temple, full of rice aroma.
Needle-shaped green tea like pine needles — Nanjing's famous tea.
scenes: 392 steps up to the Fraternity Arch — the solemn Zhongshan holy site.
The Qinhuai River of 'oar sounds and lantern shadows' — the Literary Hub arch.
Ming founder's tomb — head of the Ming-Qing imperial tombs, World Heritage.
600 years from Qing viceroy's office to Republic headquarters.
One of the three great southern lakes, ringed by the Ming wall.
First of the '480 southern temples' — cherry avenue like spring snow.
One of China's three great museums — walk through a century in the Republic hall.
The national memorial site — remember history, cherish peace.
'Qixia in autumn' — red maples and the Thousand-Buddha grottoes.
Old south-city lanes — Jinling life in grey bricks and dark tiles.
